_comment: Outside-view anchors for the Phase 7 calibration of century_sim.py. Every value is an external published estimate; ranges (not points) are used so the likelihood rewards worlds whose realised quantity falls inside the band. Signed off 2026-07-06; three end-state anchors (pandemic frequency, 2126 population, 2126 warming) added 2026-07-08. calibrate_century.py reweights the v2 ensemble toward these; CENTURY_WEIGHTS=<weights> makes century_sim.py report the anchor-weighted tables alongside the unweighted ones. The population and warming anchors are survivor-conditional (they describe worlds that avoid a global catastrophe, matching the no-collapse premise of the UN and IPCC projections), so calibrate_century.py mean-imputes non-survivors on those two features to keep the moment survivor-scoped.

extinction_by_2100.source: AI-researcher survey median P(extremely bad outcome) ~5%

nuclear_per_year.source: published great-power nuclear-war per-year estimates ~0.1%-1%/yr over ~100 yr; model base 0.3%/yr

pandemic_per_century.source: COVID-class-or-worse pandemics per century: 20th-21st century influenza pandemics (1918, 1957, 1968, 2009) plus COVID-19; Marani et al. 2021 PNAS extreme-epidemic frequency implies a few per century

population_2126_bn.source: UN World Population Prospects 2024 medium variant: global population peaks ~10.3bn around 2084 then declines; 2100 95% prediction interval ~8.9-11.6bn. Survivor-conditional (no global catastrophe)

warming_2126_C.source: IPCC AR6 WG1 (2021) 2100 best-estimate warming above 1850-1900: 1.4C (SSP1-1.9) to 4.4C (SSP5-8.5); central no-strong-mitigation SSP2-4.5 ~2.7C. Survivor-conditional (no global catastrophe)
